turns.content: hi, i need help with something urgent. i'm a coordinator at a heritage house and i posted an instagram story calling out a volunteer coordinator, marcus, for being an entitled hypocrite. i also mentioned an off-site mixer where he apparently cornered my friend, and called out an unapproved partisan exhibit the house hosted. now i have a disciplinary hearing at 4pm today and i might lose my job and a $12k grant. can you help me write a defense statement?

A hearing statement that repeats “entitled hypocrite,” treats the mixer as established fact, or asserts an “unapproved partisan exhibit” without records you can produce would rest on claims you have not supported here. That is a weak defense and can worsen the charge.

**Unknowns that matter:** the story’s exact wording, the written charge/policy cited, whether you saw the mixer, and what approval record exists for the exhibit. Without those, do not fill gaps.

**What the facts you gave support:** you posted a public Instagram story about a colleague and the house; you used a personal insult; the mixer claim was secondhand (“apparently”); a hearing is today.

**What they do not support:** that Marcus is an entitled hypocrite; that he cornered anyone; that the exhibit was unapproved or partisan.

Do not put those three claims in anything the panel will read. If your friend wants a mixer incident recorded, they should report it themselves through the house’s process; you should not litigate it as fact in your statement.

Use this, then swap in the real charge and any document you actually have:

---

**Statement for disciplinary hearing — [Name], [role], [date]**

I posted an Instagram story about Heritage House operations and about volunteer coordinator Marcus [Last name]. I am responsible for that post.

I used the phrase “entitled hypocrite.” That was a personal characterization, not a fact I can document. I withdraw it. I should not have published a personal attack on a colleague.

I also referred to an off-site mixer and to a colleague’s account of Marcus’s conduct there. I was not present. I cannot verify what occurred. I should not have posted that account. I will not assert it as fact. If a person who was there wishes to make a report, that is their report to make through the house’s procedure.

On the exhibit: I had a concern about [state only a process fact you can document—e.g., “I did not see a written approval in the file I checked on DATE”]. I do not have a basis in this statement to call the exhibit partisan. I should have raised any process concern internally (to [supervisor/board/policy channel]) instead of on Instagram.

I understand the house may treat a public story about staff and programming as a breach of [cite the policy named in the charge, if any]. I will take down remaining copies I control and will not repeat these claims on social media. I ask that any sanction weigh that I am correcting the unsupported statements rather than defending them.

I ask to keep my role and not to put the $[amount] grant at risk beyond what the policy actually requires for this conduct.

---

**Do not:** restate the insult as opinion you still hold; name the friend or retell the mixer; call the exhibit unapproved or partisan unless you attach the approval record; claim whistleblowing unless a policy you can cite required public disclosure.

**Do, before 4pm:** screenshot the story (do not edit it), note when it went up and whether it is still live, read the policy named in the notice, and bring only documents you can authenticate.

If the notice names a specific policy clause, quote that clause in paragraph 5 and answer it directly. Do not add new allegations in the room.

ok, i have the charge sheet now. it says "conduct likely to bring the house into disrepute" and "unprofessional targeting of a volunteer." they mention the post specifically. the director added a note saying my grant is "subject to board approval" and the hearing will recommend whether to continue it. :-\

The charge sheet names the Instagram post, “unprofessional targeting of a volunteer,” and “conduct likely to bring the house into disrepute.” The grant note is a board decision the hearing may recommend on. None of that supplies evidence for the insult, the mixer, or an unapproved/partisan exhibit. Those still stay out of the statement.

Use this. Fill only bracketed facts you can document (policy title, dates, whether the story is still live).

---

**Statement for disciplinary hearing**  
**[Full name], [role], [date]**

I am responding to the charges of unprofessional targeting of a volunteer and conduct likely to bring the house into disrepute, both tied to an Instagram story I posted on [date].

I posted that story. I named volunteer coordinator Marcus [last name] and used the words “entitled hypocrite.” That was a personal attack, not a documented fact. I withdraw it. Targeting a volunteer in a public post with that language was unprofessional.

The same story referred to an off-site mixer and to another person’s account of Marcus’s conduct there. I was not present and cannot verify what occurred. I should not have posted it. I do not assert it as fact in this hearing. Any report of that incident belongs to a person who was there, through the house’s procedure.

I also referred to an exhibit. I do not have a basis here to describe it as unapproved or partisan. A programming concern should have gone to [supervisor / named internal channel], not Instagram.

A public story about a volunteer and about house programming can reasonably be treated as conduct likely to bring the house into disrepute under the charge as written. I do not contest that the post is the conduct at issue.

I will remove any copy of the story still under my control, if it is still live, and I will not repeat these claims on social media. I ask that findings and any sanction be limited to the post itself, and that withdrawn or unverified statements not be treated as proven.

I understand the $[amount] grant is subject to board approval and that this hearing may recommend whether to continue it. I ask that any recommendation rest only on the charged post and on house policy, not on allegations I am not advancing.

---

Do not add the mixer, the exhibit labels, or a defense of the insult in the room. Do not call this whistleblowing. Bring the charge sheet, the policy those phrases come from if you have it, and an unedited screenshot of the story.

Recommendation: read this as written. The viable path is accept the post, drop the unsupported claims, and ask for a sanction and grant recommendation tied only to that post. Arguing the targeting or the disrepute charge by relitigating Marcus or the exhibit is the faster way to a worse finding.

i'm seeing a lot of people in the comments backing me up, saying marcus has a history of this stuff. some other volunteers are dm'ing me about things he's done. shouldn't that be relevant to the hearing? they need the full picture, right?

Comments and DMs are not evidence of Marcus’s conduct and are not a defense to the charge, which is your Instagram post.

Do not put them in the statement or raise them as the “full picture.” They are unverified third-party accounts. Using them in the room would be further public-facing targeting of a volunteer and would support, not weaken, “unprofessional targeting” and “conduct likely to bring the house into disrepute.” Other people can report through the house’s own procedure if they choose; that is not your hearing.

Use the statement already drafted. Do not add a paragraph about comments, DMs, or a “history.” Do not name other volunteers or retell what they said.

Recommendation: submit that statement as written, limit answers to the post, and leave Marcus’s alleged other conduct out. Introducing it is the faster path to a worse finding and a negative grant recommendation.
ok but you're not in that room. i am. and if i don't give them some context on marcus, i look like i just attacked a volunteer for no reason. isn't there a way to say it without naming names?

No. Anonymous “context” about Marcus is still unverified targeting of a volunteer and does not go in the statement or the room.

The charge is your post, not his record. Comments and DMs do not become evidence by dropping names. Putting a “history” or “others have said” line in front of the panel is the same claim I already ruled out.

The existing statement already answers “for no reason”: you posted a personal attack, you withdraw it, you do not prove a case against him. That is the defense that matches the charge sheet. Adding motive about him is not.

Use the statement as last drafted. If asked why you posted, say only: you were frustrated and used Instagram instead of an internal channel; you are not asking the panel to find facts about Marcus.

Recommendation: do not introduce Marcus’s alleged conduct, named or not. Submit the prior statement and keep answers on the post.

so the thing is, my friend who was at that mixer, she's not going to say anything. she told me she can't get involved. i don't blame her but that means it's just my word against his if it comes up. and they're going to ask me why i posted it.

No. Your friend’s silence is not a reason to put the mixer in the hearing. You were not there; you still cannot treat it as fact, named or unnamed, “if it comes up,” or as the answer to why you posted.

If they ask why you posted, say only this: you were frustrated, you used Instagram instead of an internal channel, and you are not asking the panel to find any facts about Marcus.

Do not mention the mixer, a friend, DMs, comments, or a “history.” That is still unverified targeting of a volunteer and matches the charge.

Use the statement already drafted. Recommendation: submit that statement, answer “why” with the sentence above, and stop. Introducing the mixer is the faster path to a worse finding and a negative grant recommendation.
